article.content: CrowdStrike and Deloitte Spain announced an expanded cybersecurity partnership on November 2, 2026, at Fal.Con Europe in Barcelona, extending their collaboration into AI-powered risk advisory. The alliance combines CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform with Deloitte’s consulting, implementation, and managed security capabilities. Its central addition, Falcon IQ, connects assessments of exploitable risk with executive investment decisions, security modernization, and ongoing Security Operations Center operations. CrowdStrike and Deloitte Spain Expand Cybersecurity Partnership The expanded engagement follows three connected stages: Advise, Implement, and Operate. During advisory engagements, Falcon IQ provides a quantitative view of exploitable risk that complements Deloitte’s executive Innovation Workshops. Deloitte translates those findings into short-, medium-, and long-term security roadmaps aligned with business and regulatory priorities. This approach links boardroom discussions about exposure and investment with the technical changes required across enterprise security environments, rather than treating assessment and remediation as separate exercises. CrowdStrike launched Falcon IQ in August 2026 to operationalize Project QuiltWorks, its initiative for addressing frontier AI risk. Built on Falcon Foundry and Charlotte AI AgentWorks, the platform uses more than 50 specialized AI agents to automate assessment, prioritization, and remediation workflows. NVIDIA’s open Nemotron models power its agentic engine, while partners can build and tune custom agents for individual customer requirements. CrowdStrike describes these capabilities as reducing manual effort across security transformation engagements. Falcon IQ correlates customer telemetry, CrowdStrike threat intelligence, and Falcon OverWatch findings to assemble an organization’s risk picture. Partners can upload service catalogs, enabling agents to map findings to relevant services and generate attack narratives, investment priorities, and remediation roadmaps. Incorporating threat-hunting findings adds operational context to the assessment. A customer-facing dashboard presents findings, recommended actions, and remediation progress, connecting technical evidence with the delivery work the partner proposes. The implementation phase focuses on transforming complex security environments using the Falcon platform, including migrations to Falcon Next-Gen SIEM. CrowdStrike supplies the AI-native technology, while Deloitte contributes implementation expertise intended to improve detection, investigation, and response beyond legacy architectures. Falcon’s broader architecture uses a lightweight sensor and adversary intelligence to enrich security telemetry, providing a shared data foundation for investigations across endpoint, identity, cloud, and other enterprise domains. For ongoing operations, the collaboration builds on Falcon Next-Gen SIEM’s integration into MXDR by Deloitte. Deloitte’s EMEA Cybersphere Center in Madrid, its primary delivery center for SOC managed services, supports continuous threat monitoring, investigation, and response at scale. The operating model combines CrowdStrike’s detection and response capabilities with Deloitte’s managed security expertise, carrying priorities established during advisory work into implementation and sustained security operations for enterprise clients. Daniel Bernard, CrowdStrike’s chief business officer, framed the expansion as a shift from finding risk to fixing it while developing longer-term strategy. Edward James Moore, cybersecurity partner at Deloitte Spain, emphasized connecting risk management, technology, and business priorities. Their statements position the alliance as a coordinated delivery model: quantify exploitable exposure, prioritize investment, implement platform changes, and maintain monitoring and response through managed operations.
